data.why: The README states the repo ships no example dataset (LasReader uses real readings only, pasted or typed by hand into the Plate Reader Assay page), so a synthetic 8x12 fluorescence plate was written in the exact paste format the page expects, with a missing well and an outlier built in for the exclusion workflow; the swarming/colony-counting tool needs an uploaded photo, which the repo doesn't provide either.

goals: Fit a weighted 4PL standard curve to AHL biosensor fluorescence standards and check its EC50, Hill slope, LOD and RMSE.
Infer each unknown sample's AHL concentration with a 95% confidence interval, scaled by its dilution factor.
Exclude a questionable standard reading with a documented reason and refit the curve.
Cross-validate the same samples read on two instruments with a log-log plot and Bland-Altman limits of agreement.
Measure colony size and spread from a photo of an agar plate for a swarming/motility assay.
Export the readings, fitted curve and inferred concentrations as CSV/PNG, since nothing is stored server-side.

review.summary: The Plate Reader Assay workflow is captured accurately and at the right grain: all 11 screens I opened match their nodes, and the run recovered the synthetic 4PL parameters after the reasoned exclusion. But the tree leaves out two of the README's three AHL tools (Cross-Validation and CAPTURE-Screen), bundles unrelated input choices in t5, and puts the separate imaging tool under the AHL goal, so it needs those fixes before filing.
